title: Membership in the Church
definition: Membership in the Church is the committed belonging of believers to a local body for worship, care, accountability, and mission.
summary: Membership in the Church is a believer's committed identification with a local congregation for care, accountability, service, and mission.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gathers His sheep into accountable communities under His shepherding care.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Membership in the church is the recognized commitment of believers to a local body for worship, care, accountability, and mission. Scripture assumes believers are known within communities where leaders shepherd and members serve one another.

Membership is not a social club roster or a way to create spiritual pride. It is a practical expression of belonging, responsibility, and mutual commitment.

Jesus gathers identifiable sheep into His flock. Church membership helps local believers take that belonging seriously in an ordered and accountable way.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because vague connection often leads to shallow care and little accountability. Membership helps answer who is being shepherded, who is committed, and who shares responsibility in the local body.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not drift around the edges of church life indefinitely. If possible, join a faithful church where you can be known, cared for, corrected, and useful in service to Christ.
